question: GQ-001
subject: a guard that could not fire, because mktemp failed and nothing checked
symptom: rebuild of 1,329 books exited 9 with MISMATCH: catalogue 1329, index 1328 — on a corpus that was entirely correct

the_corpus_was_fine.skipped_book: b19602923 — 68,649 chars of scan noise, catalogued and correctly un-indexed
the_corpus_was_fine.verified: 1 row in book_external, 0 in book_ext — the legitimate skip the guard exists to forgive

root_cause.what: BSD mktemp expands X placeholders ONLY at the end of a template
root_cause.the_line: LOGFILE=$(mktemp "/tmp/rebuild-index-XXXXXX.log") — the .log suffix made it literal
root_cause.every_run_after: mkstemp failed: File exists -> mktemp exits 1 -> LOGFILE is the EMPTY STRING
root_cause.the_silent_part: tee "" writes nowhere; grep -c PATTERN "" finds nothing; skipped=0; the forgive-an-OCR-skip branch became unreachable
root_cause.proven_not_assumed: a second mktemp on the same literal template returns empty and exits 1 — reproduced directly

why_it_hid: || echo 0 turned a broken INPUT into a plausible ANSWER — the same shape as the || true that disabled the verify chain

the_fix.template: trailing X only, plus a hard check that LOGFILE is non-empty and exists
the_fix.source_of_truth: read corpus_stats.skipped_no_paragraphs from the index (durable) before the log (per-run); -1 sentinel distinguishes "not recorded" from "zero skips"

verified_both_directions_on_the_real_scr.correct_corpus_with_an_empty_logfile: exit 0 — proves it reads corpus_stats, not the log
